subject: MSA + Order Form — pricing, min commit & invoice routing
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form — pricing follow-up

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement here — attaching the redline our legal team did to the Order Form (see Acme_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf). Two quick asks so we can move to internal approvals:

1) Can you confirm the minimum commit language — our finance team flagged the stair-step schedule and wants explicit invoice triggers per tranche.
2) Net terms: the Order Form lists Net45; accounting prefers Net30 for this vendor class. Are you able to accommodate?
3) Tax handling: will Redwood provide VAT evidence for EEA invoices? We need a certificate or process description.

Attached: Acme_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

Regards,
Sarah Jenkins
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation
[attachment: Acme_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf (pdf, 48KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Mar 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — pricing follow-up

Sarah — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Quick responses inline below; added Ben and Marissa to coordinate legal/finance handoffs.

1) Minimum commit / invoice triggers: The current Order Form ties invoice triggers to committed tranche activation dates (Section 2.1). We can add a short appendix that lists each tranche amount and the associated invoice date (e.g., 30 days after tranche activation). I'll attach a draft pricing schedule (Acme_pricing_schedule_v3.xlsx) with explicit invoice rows for each tranche so finance can map to AR.

2) Net terms: We typically operate on Net45 as standard for new accounts, but we can accept Net30 for this deal if the customer agrees to the corresponding pricing tier (we'd need a 3% adjustment on effective list rates or require payment by ACH). Before I commit, can your team confirm whether Net30 is a hard requirement or negotiable?

3) VAT evidence: Redwood will provide VAT invoices where required and can include our VAT registration and a breakdown. For EEA shipments we can supply VAT invoices and a certificate of tax residency on request. If Acme needs us to include specific invoice fields (VAT ID, reverse charge note), please flag them.

Next steps:
- I’ll upload the draft pricing schedule and a clean Order Form with an invoice-triggers appendix by EOD.
- If Ben can propose acceptable language for the Net30 concession and any payment security/escrow, we can loop in Legal for a quick redline.

Thanks — K

Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
[attachment: Acme_pricing_schedule_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Mar 2025 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — pricing follow-up

Adding procurement/finance POV. Sarah / Kimberly — quick proposal to unblock approvals:

- Net terms: Redwood can agree to Net30 if Acme signs the Order Form with the attached 3% surcharge on committed tranches (applies to first-year usage). Alternatively, we can offer Net30 with a pay-on-activation model for the first tranche only (prepay 30% as deposit) and Net45 thereafter.
- Invoice routing: We'll include explicit invoice triggers in an appendix (invoice sent to procurement@acme-corp.com and accounting@acme-corp.com) and flag which entity issues the invoice (Redwood Inc. US entity).
- Taxes: For EU invoices we will include VAT registration and a line-item for VAT; for US invoices we'll provide W-9 on request.

I attached a proposed clause for the Order Form (short paragraph we can paste into Section 2.1) and a sample invoice mapping. If Acme is OK with the surcharge, Legal can sign-off quickly; otherwise we should schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to agree tradeoffs.

Ben Carter
Principal, Commercials | Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed_net30_clause.txt (txt, 2KB)]

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 7 Mar 2025 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — pricing follow-up

Kimberly / Ben — appreciate the options. A quick update from Acme:

- Net30 is preferred but not absolute; we can accept a 1.5% surcharge rather than 3% if Redwood will commit to Net30 without prepay for tranche one. That is our finance team's compromise.
- Confirmed: invoice recipients should be procurement@acme-corp.com and accounting@acme-corp.com; please route invoices from Redwood Inc. (US entity).
- Tax evidence: we have a standard vendor onboarding checklist — we need Redwood's VAT registration (for EEA invoices) and a W-9 for US invoices. I attached our W-9 request form and included a copy of our vendor tax checklist.

Attached: W9-Acme.pdf (pdf, 12KB) — this is our vendor request form (filled by us).

Can we finalize language by Monday so I can push to legal? If you can send a clean Order Form and a tracked change version addressing the surcharge at 1.5%, we’ll route for signatures.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corporation
[attachment: W9-Acme.pdf (pdf, 12KB)]
